Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

Scope: BOTH repos, concept-driven sweep. grep -rn (tracked files only) for these removed-feature markers and report every hit that is live code or current-tense doc (not a historical note/changelog): "qemu2", "QEMU2", "handback", "hand-back", "ship.*back", "gloss_vh", "semihost" (excluding the intentional asm-fixture fallback), "verilator/" as an andesim-local path, in-tree QEMU build references, "resume leg". Also check for TODO/FIXME/XXX comments referencing already-completed migrations. Classify each hit: live legacy code vs intentional historical mention.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. - iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. # Out-of-tree build for the andesim QEMU TCG plugins. Standalone from the vsim
# CMake build because the plugins link against QEMU's plugin API + glib. Plugin
# sources live here and build here -- never inside the QEMU source tree.
#
# QEMU's plugin API header is vendored at include/qemu-plugin.h (a verbatim copy
# from the QEMU we target, currently QEMU_PLUGIN_VERSION 5), so the plugins build
# with NO QEMU source tree present -- only the built qemu-system-* binary is
# integrated externally. Re-copy the header if the target QEMU's plugin API bumps.
#
# Usage:
#   make            # build both
#   make clean
#
# Output (in this directory):
#   libhybrid_handoff.so  -- hybrid QEMU<->vsim handoff plugin (product)
#   libhotloops.so        -- hot inner-loop detector (developer profiling tool)

CC ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
# vendored qemu-plugin.h lives under include/
QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE := include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_PLUGIN_INCLUDE) $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
#   CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=<re>     assert the vsim leg's output (guest UART rides
#                              it) matches this grep -E pattern -- the hook
#                              for fixtures that verify a result INSIDE the
#                              ROI and print a verdict (code after the exit
#                              marker never runs on the vsim leg).
#   ILM_SIZE / DLM_SIZE  LM content transport override, in bytes. Unset =
#                        probe $VSIM_BIN --describe (mirrors the driver's
#                        wiring); 0 = force that memory's transport OFF
#                        (negative-control knob).
#   CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1  assert the vsim leg dumped its exit-time LM
#                        content next to its state file AND that it equals
#                        the entry-time content byte-for-byte (valid for a
#                        ROI that does not WRITE the TCM -- closes the
#                        transport loop through the real RTL SRAM).
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"

QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises

Status: draft for review
Audience: engineer running the hybrid simulator for the first time
Scope: the 2 switching modes the repo ships, with copy-paste commands,
the cycle figure each one yields, and one exercise per mode.

---

## 0. What "switching mode" means

The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:

```
   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
```

A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
that region cycle-accurately, then drains the final state. You pick
the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not
have to change between modes.

> **Two ways to invoke, one canonical.** `./andesim run` is the driver -
> the supported way to run a workload, and what the examples below lead

| # | Mode | Profiles | Switch boundary | Cycle figure it yields |
|---|------|----------|-----------------|------------------------|
| 1 | marker | a kernel | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0` (enter) / `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit) | kernel cycles |
| 2 | PC | a kernel | a PC / symbol address (no source edit) | kernel cycles |

- **Kernel modes (marker, PC)** measure ONE region you choose.

(Migration: the old M1-M8 list collapses to these 2. Old M8 - the QEMU2
semihosting exit - was removed with the QEMU2 phase, so every run now ends
at the vsim drain.)

### Where the cycle figure comes from

Every mode reads the same counter: `mcycle`, a little-endian `uint64` at
byte offset **624** in the state file (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). vsim
restores `mcycle` from QEMU1's drained value, then the RTL counts real
clock cycles, so the measured cycles are always a subtraction:

```
cycles = mcycle(vsim drain) - mcycle(QEMU1 drain)
```

The QEMU baseline cancels; only vsim's cycle-accurate delta survives. That
is why QEMU being functional-only (not cycle-accurate) does not taint the
number. marker/pc report this delta directly as the kernel cycles.
